bends.reason: Main evidence is the section across B1 (bend_01.png), measured from the plot's pixels in mm. The scan is good here: both sheet surfaces are captured 1.5 mm apart, with a clean free-edge loop at x=+11 mm that matches the CAD edge, so the bend region is visible. The scanned sheet is one straight run from x=-16 mm through the B1 locus to the free edge (slope about -3 deg, rms 0.16 mm about a single line). The change in direction at the locus is -0.3 deg on the upper surface and +1.9 deg on the lower, against +25.2 / +23.5 deg for the formed CAD. The formed CAD apex sits about 1.8 mm (more than one sheet thickness) above the scanned surface at x=0, and there are no scan points at the apex. The CAD also has an opposite crease of about 21 deg roughly 10 mm inboard. It is not a recipe bend; together with B1 it forms a joggle-like offset of about 2 mm on the 11 mm hole strip. That crease is missing from the scan too. The two missing creases nearly cancel, so the far-field roll still lies within about 0.5 mm of the blue FORMED reference and 11-16 mm from the orange reference, which unbends B1 alone. The scan's closeness to blue far from the bend therefore does not show that B1 is formed, and the orange model does not apply because the inboard crease is also unformed. The registered overlay supports this along the whole bend length: uncovered CAD appears mainly along the entire free edge of the strip in the ISO, TOP and FRONT views, while the other free edges are covered. The raw views show no distinct crease along the strip, though they are low resolution and only supporting. Caveat: only one section is provided, and the label assumes it is representative; the overlay pattern suggests it is. Note for the recipe: the CAD models this feature as a joggle (2 creases), but the recipe lists only B1.
